references.text: The seven-day consecration period for Aaron and his sons was first established in the instructions for the altar in Exodus, where it states that the consecration should last seven days.
The verse continues by explaining that they must keep watch at the Lord's tent so as not to die, which underscores the seriousness of remaining at the entrance of the tent for seven days.
A similar seven-day period is mentioned in connection with the cleansing of leprosy, where the person must remain outside the tent for seven days.
The consecration period for the Nazirites also includes a seven-day period for cleansing, showing that seven days was a common time frame for sanctification.
Ezekiel also describes a seven-day consecration period for the altar in the future temple, which mirrors the consecration in Leviticus.
The expression 'to fill the hands' (מִלֻּאֵיכֶם) refers to the consecration ritual described earlier, where priests were consecrated by having their hands filled with offerings.
